prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S685: The Common Situation Display presents the updated Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time so that operational users share the same view of the accepted change.
S686: The Departure Metering Service recalculates metering advisories after approval and prevents the swap from creating a new demand peak at a departure fix.
S687: Disputes between operators are escalated to the Regional Flow Manager when the recorded concurrences conflict or when a party alleges that governance rules were bypassed.
S688: The System Support Engineer investigates technical failures in submission, validation, or publication without altering the operational decision unless authorized through the defined control process.
S689: The Post Operations Report includes swap volume, rejection reasons, approval latency, compliance with revised times, and any equity concerns identified during the operating period.
S690: Aerodrome infrastructure events are treated as capacity inputs when they affect runway availability, taxi route usability, stand access, lighting performance, or supporting navigation services.
S691: The Regional Flow Platform records each event as an operational constraint with an effective time, expected duration, affected resource, confidence level, and approving authority.
S692: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for ensuring that declared service reductions are entered promptly and that the operational description is consistent with local aerodrome control procedures.
S693: The Tower Supervisor uses the Runway Lighting Outage Card to confirm which runway lighting elements are unavailable before approving the operational status shown in the Tower Sequence Manager.
S694: When lighting performance limits night or low-visibility operations, the Capacity Assessment Module converts the limit into a runway configuration constraint rather than treating it as a general advisory.
S695: The Airport CDM Portal presents infrastructure events to authorized airport, airline, and flow management users as part of the shared operating picture.
S696: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the published constraint when it changes the usable runway rate, taxi-out predictability, or the feasibility of the active demand plan.
S697: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates the operational effect by comparing the affected resource with the current Airport Capacity Plan and the active weather state.
S698: If the event reduces arrival throughput, the Arrival Regulation Console applies the revised Airport Acceptance Rate after confirmation by the Regional Flow Manager.
S699: If the event reduces departure throughput, the Departure Metering Service updates metering rates and provides revised inputs to the Slot Allocation Engine.
S700: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the reduced capacity value to protect fairness while avoiding schedules that exceed the declared infrastructure capability.
S701: The Demand Prediction Service recalculates short-term demand against the constrained capacity so that delay and queue forecasts reflect the published limitation.
S702: The Tower Sequence Manager displays the accepted constraint to support runway sequencing decisions and to reduce conflicting tactical instructions.
S703: The Ramp Movement Board receives the same operational status so that apron movements can be coordinated with restricted taxi routes or stand access limitations.
S704: The Common Situation Display shows the affected resource, start time, review time, and current decision status using language that can be understood by operational staff.
S705: The Alert Distribution Hub sends notifications when the constraint is created, materially changed, suspended, or cancelled.
S706: The Business Rules Registry defines which infrastructure events require approval, which events may be published as advisory information, and which events automatically trigger a Capacity Reduction State.
S707: During Adverse Weather Mode, lighting and navigation service limits are assessed together with ceiling, visibility, wind, and runway surface conditions before capacity values are released.
S708: During a Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Platform maintains the infrastructure event as a controlling assumption until an authorized actor closes or supersedes it.
S709: The Collaborative Decision Log records the time of publication, approving role, capacity effect, affected services, and any later amendment made during the operating period.
S710: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the technical record of submission, validation, publication, acknowledgement, and withdrawal for accountability and post-event review.
S711: The Data Governance Steward monitors data quality for infrastructure events, including duplicate reports, inconsistent effective times, and unclear service descriptions.
S712: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses completed infrastructure events to measure delay attribution, capacity recovery time, and the accuracy of initial duration estimates.
S713: When normal capability is restored, the Airport Duty Manager confirms closure in the Airport CDM Portal and the Regional Flow Platform returns the affected resource to Normal Operations or Recovery Phase handling as appropriate.
S714: Contingency operations cover any period in which the Regional Flow Platform cannot provide trusted automation for one or more airport, runway, apron, or airspace flow functions.
S715: A degraded operation is declared when data latency, service unavailability, or inconsistent operational outputs prevent users from relying on the normal decision support path without additional verification.
S716: The Airport Duty Manager is accountable for declaring the Contingency Fallback State after consultation with the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and System Support Engineer.
